answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent identity to solve a verifiable delay function (VDF) at registration: a puzzle that cannot be sped up by parallelism. For one honest agent the cost is a few minutes of compute; for an attacker spinning up thousands of sockpuppets it becomes an ocean of unavoidable delay. The VDF output works as a velvet rope, invisible to real users yet impossible to cut past. Because each credential binds the cipher of that exact run, identities cannot be forged or cloned, so fake accounts starve in line while genuine work moves through.
